newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bill Clinton cuddles "Chelsea" the koala.
newsitem.headline: Bill Clinton cuddles "Chelsea" the koala.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton looked, and acted, as if he were a new father on Friday when he cradled Chelsea -- a nine-month-old koala named after his daughter.
Grinning to the throng of media gathered for "The Shot" of his five-day Australian visit, Clinton talked softly to the tiny koala.
"Hey little guy meet your mommy," Clinton said to the koala as he faced "Chelsea" towards another koala.
Clinton, who looked as if he may be blushing with pride, but was probably only red-faced from the tropical sun, told reporters: "She is beautiful".
"Most people only see pictures of koalas ... I had no idea they were so soft," he told the White House press contingent.
Asked by one reporter what she thought of having a "critter" named after her 16-year-old daughter, Hillary Clinton smiled.
"We called her (Chelsea) this morning and told her we were going to see her namesake," Bill Clinton said.
On the second last day of their visit to Australia, the Clintons decided to visit a lush rainforest park -- home to kangaroos, koalas and an assortment of birds.

As the Clintons strolled through the park near this north Queensland coastal town, a ranger answered their questions about Australia's unique marsupials, at one stage telling the president that large red kangaroos would tower over his big frame.
While both Clintons patted the friendly kangaroos, only the president decided to hand feed the animals compressed grain pellets from a brown paper bag.
"They are just so sweet looking. Look at their faces and eyes," said Hillary.

The kangaroos also charmed the White House press, who once the president had left, brought out their "happy snap" cameras for family album pictures of their encounter with the strange animals from "Down Under".
